questions.q: What is the core difference between Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service?
options: They are two names for the exact same application
Desktop is a local authoring application; the service is a browser-based platform for storing, refreshing, and sharing published content
The service only works on mobile devices
Desktop is only for viewing reports; the service is only for building them
questions.explain: Desktop is where you connect, model, and build report pages. The service (app.powerbi.com) is where finished work is stored, refreshed on a schedule, and shared with people who never open Desktop.

questions.q: When you publish a .pbix file to the service, what happens to your original Desktop file?
options: It is automatically deleted from your computer
It syncs bidirectionally, so any service edit updates the Desktop file too
It stays exactly as it was — changes made to the report in the service never write back to it
It is converted into a semantic model file
questions.explain: Publishing sends the semantic model and reports to the service, but the two copies diverge immediately — edits in the service are never written back to the original .pbix file.

questions.q: Why can't you create a new workspace from inside Power BI Desktop?
options: Desktop actually can create workspaces, but only for admins
Workspace creation requires a special Desktop add-in most users don't have
Workspaces were removed from Power BI in a recent update
Workspace creation exists only in the browser-based service, by design — Desktop can publish into a workspace you already have access to, but never creates one
questions.explain: Desktop has no workspace-creation screen. The destination workspace must already exist before you publish — workspace creation, roles, and permissions are entirely a service-side concept.

questions.q: Which of the five core service concepts is NOT available inside Power BI Desktop at all?
options: Report — pages of visuals based on a semantic model
Dashboard — a single-page canvas of tiles pinned from one or more reports
DAX measures
Semantic model — tables, relationships, and measures
questions.explain: Dashboards are a service-only feature. You can build and view reports in Desktop, but dashboards — with their pinned tiles from multiple reports — only exist once content is published to the service.

questions.q: In Power BI service terminology, what is a 'consumer' or 'end user'?
options: Someone who writes DAX formulas for a semantic model
The person who installs Power BI Desktop on new laptops
A person who has admin rights over every workspace in the tenant
Someone who views and interacts with content that a designer or creator already published
questions.explain: Designers/creators build and publish content. Consumers/end users primarily view, filter, and interact with what's already been shared with them — they typically don't build or publish.
